deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the previous folio's table, now in descending order from 397 down to 5. It covers every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) below 400, followed by two summaries.

(A) Principal cycle. For each prime p, the first line lists the denominators Q_0=1, Q_1, Q_2, ... of the continued-fraction expansion of √p. The recurrences are:
- a_0 = floor(√p), P_0 = 0, Q_0 = 1;
- P_{i+1} = a_i Q_i − P_i;
- Q_{i+1} = (p − P_{i+1}^2)/Q_i;
- a_{i+1} = floor((a_0 + P_{i+1})/Q_{i+1}).

In Gauss's language (Disq. Arith. arts. 183–187, 'determinant D = p'), these Q_i are the alternating outer coefficients of the cycle of reduced forms (Q_i, P_{i+1}, −Q_{i+1}) containing the principal form (1, 0, −p).

For a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) the period of √p is odd, since x^2 − p y^2 = −1 is solvable. The Q-sequence is therefore a palindrome whose middle contains two equal consecutive terms. Gauss writes the sequence only up to that repeated pair and then '&c' (the rest is the mirror image). Two examples:
- 13: 1, 4, 3, 3 &c (full period 1, 4, 3, 3, 4, 1).
- 397: a_0 = 19, Q = 1, 36, 3, 12, 9, 4, 27, 11, 23, 12, 19, 19, with partial quotients 1, 12, 3, 4, 9, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1.

A quick test for every adjacent pair is that p − Q_i Q_{i+1} must be a perfect square, P_{i+1}^2.

(B) Further cycles. When there are further properly primitive classes of determinant p, Gauss adds a second (or third …) line. Each line is the Q-cycle of a non-principal class, written from its starting value back to that value.
- 389: 4, 7, 19, 20, 5, 13, 25, 4, with P = 19, 16, 3, 17, 18, 8, 17.
- 101: 4, 5, 13, 4.
- 37: 3, 4, 7, 3.

Such a cycle and its reverse belong to opposite (inverse) classes. So one written line stands for two classes, and h(4p) = 1 + 2·(number of extra lines). Two cases on the previous page confirm this reading:
- 401 has lines labelled 0|5, 1|4, 2|3, i.e. h = 5.
- 577 has lines labelled 0|7, 1|6, 2|5, 3|4, i.e. a cyclic class group of order 7.

On this page the primes with one extra line, hence three classes, are 37, 101, 197, 229, 257, 269, 349, 373 and 389.

(C) First summary ('Rec.'). Below 1000 there are 80 primes of the form 4n+1. The number of classes of determinant p is:
- 1 for 58 primes;
- 3 for 20 primes;
- 5 for 1 prime (401);
- 7 for 1 prime (577).

The total is 58 + 20 + 1 + 1 = 80. The 20 three-class primes are 11 on f.11r (661, 677, 701, 709, 733, 757, 761, 769, 829, 877, plus 557) and 9 on this page.

(D) Second summary ('Recapitulatio generalis'). Between 1 and 3000 there are 211 primes 4n+1. The class-number distribution is:

| classes | primes |
|---|---|
| 1 | 155 |
| 3 | 43 |
| 5 | 5 |
| 7 | 4 |
| 9 | 3 |
| 11 | 1 |

These counts also sum to 211. Implicitly, Gauss had extended the cycle computations up to 3000 on other sheets.

The point of the whole page is an empirical tabulation of class numbers of binary quadratic forms of positive prime determinant p ≡ 1 mod 4. This is the material behind Disq. Arith. art. 304 and Gauss's class-number tables for positive determinants.

I checked every adjacent pair on the page with the p − Q_iQ_{i+1} = square test. The checks pass, except for the reading of 197 noted below.
errors: 197, second line: read as '4.7.29.4' it fails, since 7·29 = 203 > 197. The correct cycle is 4, 7, 19, 4 (197−28 = 169, 197−133 = 64, 197−76 = 121). The manuscript most likely reads 19; this is a transcription issue, not Gauss's slip.
233: the line lacks the closing '&c'. This is merely notational; the sequence 1, 8, 19, 7, 16, 13, 13 is correct.
No arithmetic errors by Gauss were found in any of the sequences on this page.
The total '211' for 1 < p < 3000 is partly illegible. It agrees with the column sum 155+43+5+4+3+1 = 211, and that sum should be checked against the actual count of primes ≡ 1 mod 4 below 3000.

results.what: Period (half-period up to the central repeated pair) of the continued-fraction denominators Q_i of √p for all primes p ≡ 1 mod 4, 5 ≤ p ≤ 397; equivalently the principal cycle of reduced forms of determinant p
results.modern_name: Continued fraction of √p / cycle of reduced indefinite binary quadratic forms (infrastructure of the principal class)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange/Legendre (continued fractions and Pell), Gauss (cycles of reduced forms, Disq. Arith. 1801)

results.what: Cycles of non-principal properly primitive classes for p with h(4p) > 1 (e.g. 37, 101, 197, 229, 257, 269, 349, 373, 389), with each line standing for a class together with its opposite
results.modern_name: Computation of the form class group of discriminant 4p via cycles of reduced forms

results.what: Statistics of class numbers for prime determinants p ≡ 1 mod 4: below 1000 the counts for h = 1, 3, 5, 7 are 58, 20, 1, 1; below 3000 the counts for h = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 are 155, 43, 5, 4, 3, 1
results.modern_name: Empirical distribution of class numbers of real quadratic orders Z[√p] (precursor of Cohen–Lenstra-type heuristics / Gauss's class-number-one conjecture for real fields)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (tables and remarks in Disq. Arith. art. 304; class-number tables in Werke II)

deep.surprise_reason: These are Gauss's well-known hand computations of cycles and class numbers for positive determinants. They underlie his published observation (Disq. art. 304) that class number one is frequent for positive determinants. The worksheet detail is of archival interest but contains nothing beyond what is already attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: Consecutive products in the 397 principal cycle satisfy p − Q_iQ_{i+1} = square.
The second cycle for 389 consists of reduced forms (all differences are squares).
The correct second cycle for 197 is 4, 7, 19, 4 (not 4, 7, 29, 4).
All entries are perfect squares (289, 169, 121, 64, 49, 169, 196, 9, 289, 256, 225), validating the 349 second cycle.

checkable.sympy: len([p for p in primerange(2,1000) if p % 4 == 1]) == 80
checkable.asserts: There are 80 primes ≡ 1 mod 4 below 1000, as Gauss states.

checkable.sympy: len([p for p in primerange(2,3000) if p % 4 == 1])
checkable.asserts: Should equal 211, Gauss's 'Inter 1 et 3000 sunt 211 pr. 4n+1' (also equal to 155+43+5+4+3+1).
Internal consistency of the two summaries.

transcription_corrections: 197, second line: read '4.7.19.4 &c' (not '4.7.29.4'); the leading 4 is overwritten/underlined.
41: the line reads '1.5.5 &c' (Q_1 = 41−36 = 5, Q_2 = 5); the struck-out character is a corrected digit.
Recapitulatio: the total is most likely '211' (consistent with the column sum); the middle digit is blotted.
'(37)' at the bottom of the left column is an old page/sheet number, not part of the table.

'Rec. Infra 1000 sunt 80 n. pr. f. 4n+1' = 'Recapitulation: below 1000 there are 80 prime numbers of the form 4n+1'; the left-hand numbers 1, 3, 5, 7 (9, 11) are numbers of classes, the right-hand numbers are counts of primes.
